# Protocols & Standards

# Protocols & Standards

ThunderID is built on open identity and access standards. Each section on this page links to its own guides, with per-spec pages covering what it is, how it works, and how to enable it on your application.


### [OAuth & OIDC](https://thunderid.dev/docs/next/guides/guides/protocols/oauth-oidc.md)

The core stack for delegated authorization and federated authentication. Covers OAuth 2.1 grant types, OpenID Connect Core 1.0, client authentication, token operations, and dynamic client registration — plus security extensions such as PKCE, PAR, DPoP, and Resource Indicators.

[Browse the OAuth & OIDC catalogue →](https://thunderid.dev/docs/next/guides/guides/protocols/oauth-oidc.md)


### [Verifiable Credentials](https://thunderid.dev/docs/next/guides/guides/protocols/openid4vc.md)

Standards for requesting and verifying digital credentials held in a wallet. Covers OpenID for Verifiable Presentations (OpenID4VP): a protocol that lets a relying party request wallet-held credentials and verify them without requiring a password.

[Browse the Verifiable Credentials catalogue →](https://thunderid.dev/docs/next/guides/guides/protocols/openid4vc.md)
